important_distinctions: Throat and acoustic amplitudes are not assumed to share physical units.
Common-band features are limited to 80-3500 Hz, below the throat sensor original 4 kHz Nyquist.
The throat WAV is upsampled from 8 kHz to 16 kHz in the release; this does not create physical information above 4 kHz.
The 4000-7800 Hz energy share is acoustic-only, marked valid only when the original channel bandwidth supports it, and excluded from cross-modal RDMs.
Alignment estimates are diagnostics only; the final TAPS release already has a global alignment shift applied.
Temporal-emission features are extracted event-time landmarks from measured envelopes, not verified hidden state transitions.
Normalized interval shape is kept separate from absolute rate and dwell time; the former is affine-clock-scale invariant conditional on a fixed event set and scaled observer resolution.
The median normalized interval quantile is identically 1 by construction and is not used as an RDM feature.
Build 15 event correspondence is inferred from monotone order, within-stream mark ranks, and median-normalized interval context; it is not a known latent-state identity.
No absolute cross-observer timestamp difference is used in the event-matching objective.
Affine clock offset/rate is estimated only after correspondences are inferred; the estimate is a diagnostic and does not prove hardware synchronization.
The current alignment is order-preserving and assumes enough shared event structure; it cannot match arbitrary event reordering.
